newsitem.title: UK: Euro privatisations set to top 35 bln stg in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Euro privatisations set to top 35 bln stg in 97/98.

text.p: Over 35 billion stg of European privatisations are expected in the next two years, and these make for an appealing investment prospect, the Mercury European Privatisation Trust said on Wednesday.

Not only are giants such as France Telecom and Spanish electricity group ENDESA coming to market, but lesser known companies such as Portugal's Electricidade de Portugal (EDP), Finland's Imatran Voima Oy (IVO) and Spain's Aldeasa will be available.
"The prospects for investing in privatisations in Europe look appealing," said chairman Peter Stormonth Darling.

The trust was announcing results for the year to end-March. It said its portfolio produced a total return for the year ended March 31 of 22.8 percent against a rise of 13.8 percent in the MSCI Europe Index over the same period.
Despite the strong showing, he was disappointed that the performance was not reflected in its shares, which trade at a discount to net asset value .

"The investment manager has undertaken a series of marketing and advertising campaigns to raise public awareness of the company's performance at the portfolio level and will continue to do so, but initiatives in the past year have been hampered by a general increase in the level of investment trust discounts."
He said the trust aimed to continue buying back its ordinary shares.

Paul Harwood of investment manager Mercury Asset Management plc said the need for private investors to increase long term savings and invest in equities has only become evident recently, with interest rates on the continent at low absolute levels.

"Record levels of subscription for shares by local investors is now a feature of many continental European privatisations. Governments are playing a more appropriate role in making these assets attractive," he said.
"We have identified over 35 billion sterling of new privatisations in the next two years."
